paper.abstract_en: XYZ codes generalize the Calderbank--Shor--Steane (CSS) framework by adding $\sym{Y}$-type stabilizers to the usual $\sym{X}$- and $\sym{Z}$-type ones. We study XYZ codes whose three classical component codes are binary cyclic codes of odd length~$n$. Assigning disjoint sets of irreducible factors of $x^n-1$ to the three Pauli types fixes the number of encoded logical qubits and ensures that the row spaces of the three parity-check matrices intersect pairwise trivially. Then, a coprimality condition between the factors assigned to each type and the reciprocals of those assigned to the others guarantees the required orthogonality. Cyclotomic cosets give a complete and explicit description of the resulting family. We show that, for odd~$n$, a cyclic stabilizer code admits an XYZ representation with cyclic component codes iff its stabilizer generators are invariant, up to a phase, under the qubit permutation $i\mapsto 2i\bmod n$. By fixing the length and the dimension of the code, the proposed cyclic XYZ codes attain the best known minimum distance of stabilizer codes, exceed the minimum distance of the underlying CSS codes, and even exceed the linear-programming upper bounds for general CSS codes.
